cases.purpose: Property-check typed byte offset and count arithmetic against Rust's checked u64 reference operations.
cases.distinct_invariant: For bounded deterministic edge and arbitrary u64 pairs, typed addition and subtraction succeed exactly when checked u64 arithmetic succeeds and return the same value.
cases.expected_result: No checked typed operation wraps, panics, or disagrees with the u64 reference result.

cases.purpose: Property-check format-neutral page partitioning across bounded aligned lengths and page sizes.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every generated aligned geometry partitions its complete source into contiguous non-overlapping ranges and rejects references at and above its page count.
cases.expected_result: All valid ranges exactly cover the source and every generated boundary reference is rejected structurally.

cases.purpose: Property-check malformed zero-size and partial-page geometry inputs.
cases.distinct_invariant: Zero page size is always invalid and every non-divisible source length reports its exact generated trailing byte count.
cases.expected_result: Malformed geometry is rejected without division by zero, truncation, wrapping, or panic.

cases.purpose: Property-check every fixed-width cursor primitive against standard little-endian encoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: All generated signed, unsigned, and floating primitive bit patterns round-trip through the bounded cursor in exact byte order.
cases.expected_result: Decoded values, floating bits, final position, remaining length, and charged work all match the generated reference stream.

cases.purpose: Property-check slice random access against an independent checked range and read-budget model.
cases.distinct_invariant: For every bounded generated source, range, and budget, success, failure class, output mutation, and charged bytes agree with the model, including u64 offset overflow.
cases.expected_result: Only valid budgeted ranges copy bytes and charge work; every rejected request preserves its destination and budget.

cases.purpose: Property-check raw fixed-size page mapping and operation-wide resource bounds over generated aligned byte sources.
cases.distinct_invariant: A generated page read succeeds exactly when read, page-reference, page-visit, and aggregate-work bounds all permit it, using one persistent operation budget.
cases.expected_result: Successful reads return the exact generated page and charge one read and visit; all preflight rejections preserve output and counters.

cases.purpose: Verify copy work limits immediately around the configured boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Atomic copy work accepts one below and exact capacity and rejects one above.
cases.expected_result: Boundary outcomes are structured and the original remains safe.

cases.purpose: Verify the post-publication directory-sync failure classification.
cases.distinct_invariant: A directory-sync fault after rename reports that a validated replacement was published.
cases.expected_result: The published state is reported without claiming the original remains active.

cases.purpose: Verify every injected failure before publication.
cases.distinct_invariant: Each prepublication fault preserves original bytes and removes the private copy.
cases.expected_result: No partial replacement is exposed at any injected stage.

cases.purpose: Verify mutation and validation callback failures.
cases.distinct_invariant: Mutation and replacement-validation errors leave the original unchanged.
cases.expected_result: The callback error is structured and original bytes are preserved.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic update target preconditions.
cases.distinct_invariant: Missing and non-regular targets are rejected before private-copy mutation.
cases.expected_result: A structured target error is returned without publication.

cases.purpose: Verify the successful atomic publication path.
cases.distinct_invariant: A validated replacement is published with the original permissions preserved.
cases.expected_result: The replacement is visible only after successful validation and publication.

cases.purpose: Verify cleanup-error reporting when a primary publication error already exists.
cases.distinct_invariant: A cleanup failure is retained as secondary context without replacing the primary atomic-update error.
cases.expected_result: The primary error remains authoritative while cleanup failure details stay observable.

cases.purpose: Verify binary cursor input-size construction boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Binary cursor construction accepts exact input capacity and rejects one byte above.
cases.expected_result: Exact capacity succeeds and excess input returns a structured limit error.

cases.purpose: Verify cumulative accounting across repeated reads.
cases.distinct_invariant: Rereads consume cumulative budget and rejection does not advance cursor state.
cases.expected_result: The exhausted read fails with position and budget preserved.

cases.purpose: Verify zero-length reading at the input end.
cases.distinct_invariant: An empty read at end-of-input succeeds without charging work.
cases.expected_result: The cursor remains at the end with zero additional work.

cases.purpose: Verify successful exact-read accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: An exact read advances position and cumulative work by precisely its byte count.
cases.expected_result: Returned bytes, cursor position, and work total match the request.

cases.purpose: Verify oversized range rejection before allocation.
cases.distinct_invariant: A huge truncated range returns a structured error without allocating its claimed size.
cases.expected_result: The range fails safely with bounded work and no panic.

cases.purpose: Verify little-endian floating-point primitive decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: 32-bit and 64-bit floating reads preserve their exact IEEE bit patterns.
cases.expected_result: Decoded floating values reproduce the source bit representations.

cases.purpose: Verify signed and unsigned little-endian integer decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every supported integer width decodes exactly in little-endian order.
cases.expected_result: Decoded integer values and cursor advancement match the input bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify the single-read boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A read one byte above the per-read limit fails without advancing position.
cases.expected_result: A structured single-read limit error preserves cursor state.

cases.purpose: Verify primitive truncation behavior.
cases.distinct_invariant: A truncated fixed-width primitive read propagates error without partial advancement.
cases.expected_result: The cursor position remains unchanged after structured truncation.

cases.purpose: Verify absolute seek boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Seeking to start or exact end succeeds while seeking past end is rejected.
cases.expected_result: Valid positions are retained and the invalid seek preserves prior state.

cases.purpose: Verify structured exact-read truncation details.
cases.distinct_invariant: Truncation reports the request offset, needed bytes, and available bytes exactly.
cases.expected_result: The returned error contains complete checked boundary context.

cases.purpose: Verify strict canonical snapshot ordering checks for all protocol-declared sequences.
cases.distinct_invariant: Tables, columns, indexes, rows, and relationships are each rejected when their declared canonical ordering is violated.
cases.expected_result: Every unordered sequence returns a structured error identifying its semantic path.

cases.purpose: Verify explicit canonicalization of every protocol-declared sequence.
cases.distinct_invariant: One explicit operation sorts tables, columns, indexes, rows, and relationships without changing undeclared sequence semantics.
cases.expected_result: Canonicalized state and canonicalized output have the exact declared ascending orders.

cases.purpose: Verify unique identity requirements enforced by the executable protocol validator.
cases.distinct_invariant: Duplicate table names, column ordinals or names, index names, and relationship names fail closed after sorting.
cases.expected_result: Every duplicate identity returns a structured error containing its semantic path and duplicated value.

cases.purpose: Verify Unicode code-point ordering of dynamic JSON object keys.
cases.distinct_invariant: ASCII, accented BMP, and supplementary-plane keys are emitted in Unicode code-point ascending order.
cases.expected_result: Canonical JSON places the representative keys in exact protocol order without ASCII escaping.

cases.purpose: Verify retention of protocol sequences that have no sorting declaration.
cases.distinct_invariant: Index fields, relationship field pairs, and raw-preservation records retain producer-declared order.
cases.expected_result: Canonical output preserves the exact supplied order of all three sequence kinds.

cases.purpose: Verify required nested string and collection constraints.
cases.distinct_invariant: Empty DAO types, index fields, relationship fields, raw semantic paths, and raw purposes are rejected at their precise locations.
cases.expected_result: Each malformed nested shape returns a structured empty-string or empty-collection error.

cases.purpose: Verify exact protocol constants, object-key order, compactness, and line termination for an empty snapshot.
cases.distinct_invariant: The minimal typed model emits the complete protocol 1.0.0 canonical snapshot byte sequence with one trailing LF.
cases.expected_result: Emitted bytes exactly equal the checked compact UTF-8 JSON document.

cases.purpose: Verify all fifteen canonical typed-value discriminants and representations.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every protocol value kind has a distinct kind tag and correctly typed semantic value, with optional fields in canonical key order.
cases.expected_result: Canonical output contains the exact representation for each typed value kind.

cases.purpose: Verify the required distinction among SQL null, empty text, and empty binary.
cases.distinct_invariant: The three semantically distinct values retain different typed canonical JSON despite having no content.
cases.expected_result: Null emits JSON null while text and binary emit empty strings under distinct kind tags.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical UTF-8 string escaping across controls, syntax characters, and non-ASCII scalars.
cases.distinct_invariant: Required controls are minimally escaped while accented and supplementary Unicode remain direct UTF-8.
cases.expected_result: The exact compact escape sequences are present without ASCII-only or surrogate escaping.

cases.purpose: Verify finite numeric normalization and non-finite rejection.
cases.distinct_invariant: Negative zero, fixed, scientific, and large integral finite values emit normalized JSON while NaN and infinities cannot enter the model.
cases.expected_result: Finite values have exact deterministic number text and all non-finite constructors return structured errors.

cases.purpose: Verify lowercase hexadecimal and hyphenated GUID grammar.
cases.distinct_invariant: Only even-length lowercase hexadecimal text and exact lowercase GUID shapes are constructible.
cases.expected_result: Valid boundary representations succeed and uppercase, odd, malformed, or non-hex inputs fail structurally.

cases.purpose: Verify invariant decimal, currency, and timezone-free date/time grammar.
cases.distinct_invariant: Accepted and rejected boundary strings match the executable protocol validator's representation rules.
cases.expected_result: Only invariant decimal and timezone-free ISO-shaped date/time strings are constructible.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot scenario, database hash, and producer revision boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Scenario family grammar, lowercase SHA-256 length, and Unicode producer revision length are enforced before emission.
cases.expected_result: Accepted protocol boundaries construct exactly and every malformed identity returns its specific structured error.

cases.purpose: Verify deterministic canonical snapshot byte equality.
cases.distinct_invariant: Repeated strict serialization, clone serialization, and explicit canonicalized serialization produce identical retained bytes.
cases.expected_result: All three independently requested byte vectors are exactly equal.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical row ordering when producer-declared keys are not unique.
cases.distinct_invariant: Rows sharing one key sort by canonical values while semantically identical duplicate rows remain retained.
cases.expected_result: Strict emission rejects reversed values, explicit canonicalization orders them, and identical duplicates survive.

cases.purpose: Verify public error display context.
cases.distinct_invariant: Formatted structured errors retain the operation and boundary context needed for diagnosis.
cases.expected_result: The display text includes the structured error's relevant fields.

cases.purpose: Verify classification of every documented generic Jet file signature.
cases.distinct_invariant: Standard, system, and temporary signatures map to their respective typed file kinds.
cases.expected_result: Each documented signature returns the exact corresponding Jet file kind.

cases.purpose: Verify the physical location of the Jet signature.
cases.distinct_invariant: Signature classification reads from byte offset four independently of unrelated leading bytes.
cases.expected_result: Every leading-byte pattern still yields the documented standard-file classification.

cases.purpose: Verify matching of signatures shorter than the complete observation window.
cases.distinct_invariant: System and temporary classification depends only on their documented literal prefixes, not unspecified suffix bytes.
cases.expected_result: Varied suffix bytes preserve the appropriate system or temporary classification.

cases.purpose: Verify significance of every byte in each documented signature literal.
cases.distinct_invariant: Mutating any documented signature byte prevents that signature from matching.
cases.expected_result: Every single-byte mutation returns an unknown-signature error containing the mutation.

cases.purpose: Verify diagnostic preservation for an unrecognized Jet signature.
cases.distinct_invariant: Unknown-signature errors retain all fifteen observed signature bytes without loss.
cases.expected_result: The structured error contains the complete rejected observation.

cases.purpose: Verify every truncation length before the complete signature window.
cases.distinct_invariant: Lengths before offset four report out-of-bounds, while later incomplete windows report exact unexpected-end context.
cases.expected_result: Every truncated input returns the precise structured boundary error without panic.

cases.purpose: Verify signature reading at the exact resource budget.
cases.distinct_invariant: A budget equal to the fifteen-byte signature window permits classification and charges exactly fifteen bytes.
cases.expected_result: Classification succeeds and cumulative read work equals the window length.

cases.purpose: Verify the signature reader's per-read budget boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A single-read budget one byte below the signature window rejects the read without charging work.
cases.expected_result: A structured single-read limit error is returned and total read work remains zero.

cases.purpose: Verify the signature reader's cumulative-read budget boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A total-read budget one byte below the signature window rejects the read without charging work.
cases.expected_result: A structured total-read limit error is returned and cumulative work remains zero.

cases.purpose: Verify public diagnostics and source chaining for header failures.
cases.distinct_invariant: Read failures expose their structured source while unknown signatures remain source-free and both display useful context.
cases.expected_result: Error displays identify the failure and standard error chaining preserves only the underlying read error.

cases.purpose: Verify Jet 3 geometry for an exact one-page source.
cases.distinct_invariant: A 2,048-byte source derives one page with the fixed Jet 3 page size.
cases.expected_result: Geometry reports the exact source length, page size, and page count.

cases.purpose: Verify Jet 3 geometry for an aligned multi-page source.
cases.distinct_invariant: A 4,096-byte source derives exactly two fixed-size Jet 3 pages.
cases.expected_result: Geometry reports the aligned source length and exact two-page count.

cases.purpose: Verify rejection of a source with a trailing partial Jet 3 page.
cases.distinct_invariant: Geometry rejects one trailing byte beyond a complete page using source length alone and consumes no read budget.
cases.expected_result: A structured partial-page error reports the single trailing byte while total read work remains zero.

cases.purpose: Verify page-reader construction for empty and aligned source lengths.
cases.distinct_invariant: Construction derives zero-page and three-page Jet 3 geometry from captured length without reading the source.
cases.expected_result: Both aligned geometries report the fixed 2,048-byte page size and zero source reads.

cases.purpose: Verify page-reader rejection of a trailing partial page.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source one byte longer than a complete 2,048-byte page is rejected from its length before page access.
cases.expected_result: A structured partial-page error reports the source length, fixed page size, and one trailing byte.

cases.purpose: Verify raw reads at both ends of aligned page geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: Page zero and the last page of a three-page source map to their exact non-overlapping 2,048-byte regions.
cases.expected_result: Both complete pages are returned and exactly two reads, page visits, and work units are charged.

cases.purpose: Verify page-reference rejection immediately beyond aligned geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: References equal to the two-page count and one above it fail before source access or resource charging.
cases.expected_result: Both references return structured page-bounds errors with all counters and source reads at zero.

cases.purpose: Verify raw page access against empty geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: Page zero is outside a zero-page source and its rejection performs no read or resource charge.
cases.expected_result: A structured page-bounds error reports zero pages while every counter remains unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify preflight ordering between read limits and page geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: An insufficient single-read budget takes precedence over an invalid page reference and leaves all accounting untouched.
cases.expected_result: The single-read limit error is returned before bounds access, source I/O, or resource charging.

cases.purpose: Verify a complete raw page read at exact byte limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: Single-read and cumulative-read ceilings equal to 2,048 bytes permit exactly one complete page read.
cases.expected_result: The read succeeds and charges exactly 2,048 read bytes and one page visit.

cases.purpose: Verify the raw page reader's per-read byte boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A single-read ceiling one byte below the 2,048-byte page size rejects access atomically.
cases.expected_result: A structured single-read limit error is returned with no source read or resource charge.

cases.purpose: Verify the raw page reader's cumulative-byte boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A cumulative-read ceiling one byte below the 2,048-byte page size rejects access atomically.
cases.expected_result: A structured total-read limit error is returned with no source read or resource charge.

cases.purpose: Verify cumulative accounting across repeated raw page reads.
cases.distinct_invariant: After one 2,048-byte page read exhausts the cumulative ceiling, rereading that page fails before a second visit.
cases.expected_result: The second read returns a cumulative limit error and preserves the first read's counters.

cases.purpose: Verify page-visit accounting at its exact boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A one-visit ceiling permits the first raw page read and rejects the second before source access or read charging.
cases.expected_result: The second read returns a page-visit limit error while counters retain exactly one completed visit.

cases.purpose: Verify aggregate work accounting at its exact boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A one-unit total-work ceiling permits the first raw page read and rejects the second without partial accounting.
cases.expected_result: The second read returns a total-work limit error while read, visit, and work totals remain at one page.

cases.purpose: Verify raw page-reader behavior when the source returns a short read.
cases.distinct_invariant: A short source read charges the attempted 2,048 bytes and page visit but does not expose a partial destination update.
cases.expected_result: The structured short-read error preserves exact byte counts, charged work, and the original destination bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify raw page-reader behavior when source I/O fails.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source I/O fault charges the attempted page read and visit but leaves the caller's destination unchanged.
cases.expected_result: The structured I/O error is propagated with one charged read and visit and no destination mutation.

cases.purpose: Verify recovery of the page reader's owned source.
cases.distinct_invariant: Consuming an unused page reader returns the original aligned source with its bytes and zero-read state intact.
cases.expected_result: The extracted source retains one complete page of bytes and records no reads.

cases.purpose: Verify format-neutral default read limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: Default input, single-read, and cumulative-read limits match the documented policy.
cases.expected_result: Every default equals its documented numeric constant.

cases.purpose: Verify explicitly configured read limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: Zero, unit, and maximum explicit read-policy values are preserved exactly.
cases.expected_result: Policy accessors return each supplied boundary unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify successful read-budget charges.
cases.distinct_invariant: Zero and exact-boundary charges update cumulative work without overcharging.
cases.expected_result: The work total equals the sum of accepted charges.

cases.purpose: Verify input-length policy boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Input length at the ceiling succeeds and one byte above is rejected.
cases.expected_result: The over-limit result identifies requested and maximum bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify cumulative read counter overflow handling.
cases.distinct_invariant: Cumulative read addition overflow returns arithmetic error without wrapping or mutation.
cases.expected_result: The counter retains its prior value after overflow rejection.

cases.purpose: Verify failed read charges are atomic.
cases.distinct_invariant: Single-read and cumulative-limit rejection never charges partial work.
cases.expected_result: Both failure paths preserve the pre-request work total.

cases.purpose: Verify checked byte-count boundary arithmetic.
cases.distinct_invariant: Byte-count addition and subtraction accept exact representable boundaries.
cases.expected_result: Checked count operations return the exact boundary values.

cases.purpose: Verify invalid byte-count arithmetic.
cases.distinct_invariant: Byte-count overflow and underflow return structured arithmetic errors.
cases.expected_result: No count operation wraps or panics.

cases.purpose: Verify native-size conversions for typed offsets and counts.
cases.distinct_invariant: Representable native-sized values round-trip through typed byte values exactly.
cases.expected_result: Conversion returns the original representable value.

cases.purpose: Verify checked byte-offset boundary arithmetic.
cases.distinct_invariant: Byte-offset arithmetic accepts the last exact representable result.
cases.expected_result: Checked offset operations return exact boundary positions.

cases.purpose: Verify invalid byte-offset arithmetic.
cases.distinct_invariant: Byte-offset overflow and underflow fail structurally without wrapping.
cases.expected_result: Invalid offset math returns a checked arithmetic error.

cases.purpose: Verify absolute page-offset addition overflow.
cases.distinct_invariant: Adding a local page offset to an absolute start cannot wrap.
cases.expected_result: Overflow returns a structured arithmetic error.

cases.purpose: Verify page references against empty geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: An empty source geometry rejects page reference zero.
cases.expected_result: The first reference is identified as outside the zero-page database.

cases.purpose: Verify page-count derivation at exact file boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Exact multiples of page size derive the corresponding complete page count.
cases.expected_result: Geometry reports the precise number of full pages and no partial page.

cases.purpose: Verify local page offset boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: The last byte is valid while exact page end and one byte above are invalid local offsets.
cases.expected_result: Boundary validation distinguishes addressable bytes from end positions.

cases.purpose: Verify partial-page geometry around exact capacity.
cases.distinct_invariant: File lengths one below and one above a full-page boundary are identified as partial.
cases.expected_result: Complete page count and trailing byte count are exact on both sides.

cases.purpose: Verify calculated byte ranges for boundary pages.
cases.distinct_invariant: First and last valid page ranges cover their exact non-overlapping source bytes.
cases.expected_result: Calculated start and end offsets match database geometry.

cases.purpose: Verify page-number multiplication overflow.
cases.distinct_invariant: Page-number to byte-offset multiplication cannot wrap.
cases.expected_result: An unrepresentable page start returns a structured arithmetic error.

cases.purpose: Verify page references immediately beyond valid count.
cases.distinct_invariant: References equal to page count and one above are both rejected.
cases.expected_result: Each invalid reference reports the available page count.

cases.purpose: Verify page geometry uses captured source length.
cases.distinct_invariant: Page geometry construction observes only the source length captured at source creation.
cases.expected_result: Later source changes cannot silently alter established geometry.

cases.purpose: Verify typed page number, size, and offset boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Typed page values preserve zero and maximum representable valid boundaries.
cases.expected_result: Constructed page values return their exact source integers.

cases.purpose: Verify typed page conversion overflow.
cases.distinct_invariant: Native conversion of unrepresentable page values fails rather than truncating.
cases.expected_result: Conversion returns a structured arithmetic error.

cases.purpose: Verify the nonzero page-size invariant.
cases.distinct_invariant: Zero page size is invalid for both empty and populated sources.
cases.expected_result: Geometry construction rejects zero before division or allocation.

cases.purpose: Verify aggregate resource-work rejection atomicity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Aggregate work rejection preserves every individual resource counter.
cases.expected_result: No dimension is partially charged by an aggregate failure.

cases.purpose: Verify allocation accounting boundaries and aggregation.
cases.distinct_invariant: Allocation accepts exact capacity while one-over and aggregate failures are atomic.
cases.expected_result: Rejected allocations leave both allocation and total-work counters unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify traversal chain-depth boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Exact chain depth succeeds and one-over fails without mutating accounting.
cases.expected_result: Depth validation returns a structured limit error at one above.

cases.purpose: Verify decoded-value size accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: Single-value and cumulative decoded-byte ceilings are enforced independently.
cases.expected_result: Each exceeded dimension reports its own structured limit kind.

cases.purpose: Verify comprehensive resource-policy defaults.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every parser resource default matches the documented numeric policy.
cases.expected_result: All public default accessors equal their documented constants.

cases.purpose: Verify overflow handling for all cumulative resource counters.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every cumulative counter rejects u64 overflow without mutation.
cases.expected_result: No resource counter wraps or partially advances.

cases.purpose: Verify parsed-item and aggregate-work boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Item work accepts exact capacity while local and aggregate excess fail atomically.
cases.expected_result: Rejected item charges preserve all relevant counters.

cases.purpose: Verify page-visit and aggregate-work boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Page visits accept exact capacity while local and aggregate excess fail atomically.
cases.expected_result: Rejected visits do not change page or total-work counters.

cases.purpose: Verify integration between operation and read budgets.
cases.distinct_invariant: The read budget persists as a sub-budget and contributes to operation work.
cases.expected_result: Read accounting remains visible through the enclosing operation budget.

cases.purpose: Verify total-work capacity and aggregation.
cases.distinct_invariant: Total work accepts exact capacity while one-over and combined excess fail atomically.
cases.expected_result: Failed charges preserve the previous total and dimensional counters.

cases.purpose: Verify the public format-name scope.
cases.distinct_invariant: The library identifies only Access 97 and Jet 3 as its target format.
cases.expected_result: The public format name exactly matches the declared narrow scope.

cases.purpose: Verify slice and file out-of-range parity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Slice-backed and file-backed sources reject identical invalid ranges equivalently.
cases.expected_result: Both source types return the same structured boundary class.

cases.purpose: Verify empty source geometry and reading.
cases.distinct_invariant: Empty sources retain zero geometry and accept only an empty read at the end.
cases.expected_result: Slice and file sources agree without charging work.

cases.purpose: Verify file-source input length limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: File source construction accepts exact file capacity and rejects one byte above.
cases.expected_result: Oversize files return a structured input limit error.

cases.purpose: Verify stable file-source length.
cases.distinct_invariant: File length is captured once and later growth is not exposed through established geometry.
cases.expected_result: Reads beyond the captured length remain rejected.

cases.purpose: Verify source range arithmetic preflight.
cases.distinct_invariant: Offset-plus-length overflow is rejected before any underlying source access.
cases.expected_result: A structured arithmetic error is returned with zero I/O.

cases.purpose: Verify missing-file open diagnostics.
cases.distinct_invariant: Opening a missing source maps the platform failure to structured I/O context.
cases.expected_result: The error identifies the open operation and not-found kind.

cases.purpose: Verify source preflight accounting atomicity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Single and total read-limit failures leave the source budget unchanged.
cases.expected_result: No rejected preflight request consumes read budget.

cases.purpose: Verify successful slice/file source parity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Slice-backed and file-backed sources return identical bytes for identical valid ranges.
cases.expected_result: Returned bytes and work totals match across source implementations.

cases.purpose: Verify slice-source input length limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: Slice source construction accepts exact capacity and rejects one byte above.
cases.expected_result: Oversize slices return a structured input limit error.

cases.purpose: Verify shared operation accounting across readers.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source and binary cursor share and exhaust one enclosing operation budget.
cases.expected_result: Combined work cannot bypass the operation ceiling.

cases.purpose: Verify file truncation after length capture.
cases.distinct_invariant: A later-truncated file reports actual short-read bytes and charges attempted I/O.
cases.expected_result: The structured short-read error and budget reflect the failed access.

cases.purpose: Verify file-source random access initialization.
cases.distinct_invariant: Wrapping an open file is independent of its preexisting stream cursor position.
cases.expected_result: Absolute reads return the intended bytes regardless of prior cursor state.

cases.purpose: Verify testkit fixture format metadata.
cases.distinct_invariant: Fixture metadata derives its format name from the production library scope.
cases.expected_result: Testkit and library report exactly the same scoped format name.
